countries.name: Saudi Arabia & Gulf States

traditions.name: Iftar Cannon
traditions.description: Traditional cannon fire signals time to break fast in many cities

traditions.name: Ghabga
traditions.description: Late-night social gatherings and feasts after Taraweeh prayers

traditions.name: Ramadan Tents
traditions.description: Elaborate outdoor tents set up for communal iftars and charity meals

countries.specialNote: Night markets (souqs) stay open late into the night during Ramadan

cities.name: Riyadh
iftar_meals: thareed (bread soaked in lamb and vegetable stew)
kabsa (spiced rice with chicken or lamb)
rituals_and_traditions: Large family and tribal gatherings
Night prayers (taraweeh) with packed mosques
cities.notes: Thareed is a classic Saudi iftar stew, while kabsa is a national dish popular in Ramadan.

cities.name: Jeddah
suhoor_meals: similar to Riyadh with more seafood options
rituals_and_traditions: Coastal city gatherings with extended families
Charity iftars near major mosques
cities.notes: Jeddah shares core Saudi Ramadan dishes with additional Red Sea seafood.

countries.name: Egypt

traditions.name: Fanous
traditions.description: Colorful decorative lanterns hung in homes and streets

traditions.name: Mesaharati
traditions.description: Traditional drum beater who wakes people for Suhoor by walking through neighborhoods

traditions.name: Ramadan TV Series
traditions.description: Special television dramas produced exclusively for Ramadan

traditions.name: Charity Tables
traditions.description: Free iftar tables set up in streets for the needy

countries.specialNote: Egypt is famous for its elaborate Ramadan lanterns that light up streets and homes

cities.name: Cairo
rituals_and_traditions: Fanoos (Ramadan lanterns) decorating streets and homes
Lanterns carried by children while singing Ramadan songs
Family iftars that often extend into late-night socializing
cities.notes: Colorful fanoos lanterns and ful with karkadeh are widely associated with Egyptian Ramadan.

cities.name: Alexandria
iftar_meals: seafood dishes alongside standard Egyptian iftar items
rituals_and_traditions: Coastal iftars with extended families
Neighborhood lantern displays similar to Cairo
cities.notes: Coastal influence adds more fish/seafood to otherwise typical Egyptian Ramadan meals.

countries.name: Morocco

traditions.name: Harira Tradition
traditions.description: Breaking fast with harira soup, dates, and chebakia (sesame cookies)

traditions.name: Neffar
traditions.description: Similar to mesaharati, calls people to suhoor with horn or flute

countries.specialNote: Hand of Fatima decorations are traditionally displayed during Ramadan

cities.name: Casablanca
suhoor_meals: bread with olive oil and cheese
rituals_and_traditions: Family-centered iftar centered around harira
Traditional clothing like djellaba and kaftan for prayers and gatherings
cities.notes: Harira, rfissa, and tangia are highlighted as signature Moroccan Ramadan dishes.

cities.name: Marrakesh
suhoor_meals: bread, olive oil, and local cheeses
iftar_meals: rfissa (chicken and lentils over shredded bread)
rituals_and_traditions: Large family gatherings after Maghrib
Old city squares buzzing at night with food stalls
cities.notes: Tanjia Marrakchia is particularly linked to Marrakesh Ramadan tables.

countries.name: Turkey

traditions.name: Mahya
traditions.description: Lights strung between minarets forming messages and designs

traditions.name: Drummers
traditions.description: Traditional drummers walk neighborhoods for Suhoor wake-up calls

countries.specialNote: Special flatbread (Pide) is baked only during Ramadan

cities.name: Istanbul
iftar_meals: Ramazan pidesi (special Ramadan flatbread) with meat or vegetable dishes
rituals_and_traditions: Mosques hang mahya (illuminated messages) between minarets
Public iftar tents by municipalities
Street drummers waking people for suhoor in some districts
cities.notes: Ramazan pidesi is a special bread baked only in Ramadan and widely eaten for iftar and sahur.

cities.name: Ankara
iftar_meals: Ramazan pidesi with stews and kebabs
rituals_and_traditions: Mahya lights on major mosques
Municipal iftar programs
cities.notes: Patterns are similar nationwide with local variations in main dishes.

countries.name: Lebanon

traditions.name: Iftar Cannon
traditions.description: Iftar cannons signal sunset; family and neighborhood gatherings

countries.specialNote: Iftar cannons are a long-standing tradition used to mark the end of each fasting day.

cities.name: Beirut
iftar_meals: rice with stews and grilled meats
rituals_and_traditions: Midfa al-iftar (iftar cannons) to signal sunset
Family and neighborhood gatherings
cities.notes: Iftar cannons are a long-standing tradition used to mark the end of each fasting day.

countries.name: Jordan

traditions.name: Mansaf at Ramadan
traditions.description: Mansaf at large family gatherings and special Ramadan occasions

countries.specialNote: Mansaf, Jordan's national dish, is central to celebrations and gatherings, including Ramadan.

cities.name: Amman
iftar_meals: mansaf (lamb with rice and jameed yogurt)
rituals_and_traditions: Mansaf at large family gatherings and special Ramadan occasions
cities.notes: Mansaf, Jordan's national dish, is central to celebrations and gatherings, including Ramadan.

countries.name: Indonesia & Malaysia

traditions.name: Bedug Drums
traditions.description: Large drums beaten at mosques to announce iftar and prayer times

traditions.name: Ramadan Markets
traditions.description: Night bazaars selling traditional foods and drinks

traditions.name: Mudik Tradition
traditions.description: Mass exodus to hometowns to spend Ramadan with family

countries.specialNote: Takjil - small snacks and drinks given out for free at iftar time

cities.name: Jakarta
iftar_meals: kolak (sweet banana, coconut, palm sugar dessert)
rituals_and_traditions: Nyekar/nyadran style grave visits and prayers in some Javanese communities before Ramadan
Crowded street food markets (pasar Ramadan) each evening
cities.notes: Indonesian Ramadan includes cemetery visits (nyekar/nyadran) and abundant sweet snacks at iftar.

cities.name: Yogyakarta
rituals_and_traditions: Padusan ritual cleansing in springs or lakes before Ramadan
Javanese cultural elements woven into pre-Ramadan observances
cities.notes: Padusan is a Javanese ritual cleansing used to welcome Ramadan.

cities.name: Aceh
suhoor_meals: rice and fish or meat dishes
iftar_meals: meugang meat dishes (beef, goat, or buffalo) eaten around start of Ramadan
rituals_and_traditions: Meugang, a communal meat feast with family just before Ramadan begins
cities.notes: Meugang is a distinctive Acehnese pre-Ramadan meat feast.

countries.name: Pakistan & India

traditions.name: Rooh Afza
traditions.description: Traditional rose syrup drink consumed widely during iftar

traditions.name: Shab-e-Qadr
traditions.description: Special night vigils in last ten days with Quran recitation

traditions.name: Chaand Raat
traditions.description: Night before Eid with shopping, henna, and celebrations

countries.specialNote: Dastarkhwan - large communal cloth spread on floor for iftar gatherings

cities.name: Karachi
rituals_and_traditions: Bustling iftar bazaars selling fried snacks
Charity iftar tables along main roads
Chaand raat shopping before Eid with henna and bangles
cities.notes: Iftar in Pakistan commonly features fried snacks, rose-flavored drinks, and haleem; chaand raat is a key end-of-Ramadan celebration.

cities.name: Lahore
suhoor_meals: paratha and nihari or other meat stews
rituals_and_traditions: Old-city food streets packed after iftar
Strong communal culture around late-night eating
cities.notes: Lahore's Ramadan is famous for its food streets and rich meaty dishes.

countries.name: Bangladesh

traditions.name: Taraweeh at Baitul Mukarram

countries.specialNote: Historic communal iftar traditions in Chawk Bazaar area of Old Dhaka
